configKeys.effect: Mod ids that switch the trigger off when installed, checked once in common setup via ModList.isLoaded. Empty on purpose - nothing in the current pack collides. The known candidate is 'iteminteractions', the library behind Easy Shulker Boxes, which hooks the same ScreenEvent.MouseButtonPressed.Pre on container screens. A list rather than a hard-coded set so a collision can be defused without a release.

Whether a right-click on a crafting table in the player's own inventory opens the grid - from the survival inventory and from any container screen except a crafting screen, in survival and adventure only. Turning it off leaves the module and its server side loaded but removes the trigger, which is the setting to reach for when another mod claims the same click. Read live by the client handler, so it takes effect without a restart.

Only fire while the mouse cursor carries nothing. Also what keeps Mouse Tweaks out of the way: its right-click drag only arms when the cursor is holding something, so an empty cursor is the one branch where the two cannot collide.

Make stillValid() check that a crafting table is still in the main inventory or the offhand, closing the grid when it is not. Off by default because the 3x3 grid is a TransientCraftingContainer and not part of Inventory: a player who legitimately puts the table into the grid as an ingredient would read as having none and the menu would close mid-craft. Nothing is lost either way - removed() always empties the grid back into the inventory.

configKeys.defaultValue: generic_9x1..9x6, generic_3x3, shulker_box, hopper, furnace, blast_furnace, smoker, brewing_stand (all minecraft:)
configKeys.effect: Menu types the grid may send the player back into after Escape; anything else returns to the survival inventory. An allow-list on purpose: going back means replaying the recorded MenuProvider a second time, and a provider is not obliged to survive that - one that built a temporary entity to back its screen (Overpacked's backpack bridge) would point at a discarded entity, and its client factory dereferences that without a null check, which NeoForge answers by disconnecting the client. The defaults are vanilla containers backed by a block entity, an entity or the ender chest inventory, none of which reads extra data on the client.

Escape or the inventory key goes back to where the grid was opened from: the survival inventory, or the container that was open if its menu type is listed in return_menu_types (anything else falls back to the inventory). Off means Escape behaves like a real table and lands in the world. Only covers closing it yourself: a close forced by the server arrives as a packet and never runs through Screen.onClose().

Add a "Right-click to open" line to a crafting table's tooltip. Drawn exactly where the click works - a table in the player's own inventory, in any eligible container screen, in survival or adventure - because the tooltip and the trigger share one eligibility check. A table in the chest half, the creative menu or a recipe viewer gets no line.

events: net.neoforged.neoforge.network.event.RegisterPayloadHandlersEvent (mod event bus; getModEventBus().addListener(this::onRegisterPayloadHandlers) in onInitialize, PocketCraftingModule.java). Registers both C2S requests (open_pocket_crafting, return_from_pocket_crafting) on registrar "1" with .optional().

net.neoforged.neoforge.client.event.ScreenEvent.MouseButtonPressed.Pre (game event bus, client only; @EventBusSubscriber on PocketCraftingClientEvents). The trigger: right-click on a crafting table in the player's own inventory, in any AbstractContainerScreen except a CraftingScreen. Cancels the event so the click is not also handled as a slot pickup.

net.neoforged.neoforge.client.event.ScreenEvent.Opening (game event bus, client only; PocketCraftingClientEvents). Swaps the stock CraftingScreen for PocketCraftingScreen when the menu title marks it as ours.

net.neoforged.neoforge.event.entity.player.ItemTooltipEvent (game event bus, client only; PocketCraftingClientEvents). Appends the "Right-click to open" hint, gated by the same eligibleSlot() check the trigger uses: the hovered slot must hold a crafting table, belong to the player's own Inventory, in an AbstractContainerScreen that is not a CraftingScreen, with the player in survival or adventure.
net.neoforged.neoforge.event.entity.player.PlayerEvent.PlayerLoggedOutEvent (game event bus; NeoForge.EVENT_BUS.register(this) in onInitialize). Drops the player's pending return target.
notes:
NO ASSETS OF OUR OWN, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE DESIGN. PocketCraftingMenu extends net.minecraft.world.inventory.CraftingMenu instead of registering a menu type. AbstractContainerMenu.menuType is assigned once in the protected constructor and getType() only reads it, so the subclass still reports MenuType.CRAFTING - which is what ServerPlayer.openMenu puts into ClientboundOpenScreenPacket. Any client, including a vanilla one, therefore builds the stock CraftingScreen (MenuScreens registers MenuType.CRAFTING -> CraftingScreen::new). No DeferredRegister, no RegisterMenuScreensEvent, no texture, and every recipe viewer in the pack (EMI, Not Enough Recipe Book, TooManyRecipeViewers) sees a crafting screen it already understands. The only language keys added are the menu title, in two variants (see TWO TITLE KEYS below), and the tooltip hint.

THE CONTAINERLEVELACCESS TRAP. CraftingMenu(int, Inventory) delegates to ContainerLevelAccess.NULL, whose evaluate() never invokes the function it is handed, and whose execute() is a default method built on evaluate(). With NULL, two things in the superclass silently break: slotsChanged() never reaches slotChangedCraftingGrid, so the result slot is never computed and the grid is inert; and removed(Player) never reaches clearContainer, so the nine items in the grid are destroyed when the screen closes. So a real access is required - ContainerLevelAccess.create(level, player.blockPosition()). Only the level is ever used by the superclass (slotChangedCraftingGrid asks it for the recipe manager, onCraftedBy takes it); the position is read exclusively by the inherited stillValid, which is overridden.

STILLVALID MUST BE OVERRIDDEN. The inherited implementation is AbstractContainerMenu.stillValid(access, player, Blocks.CRAFTING_TABLE), which looks for a crafting table block at the access position. There is none - that is the point of the module - so Player.tick() would close the menu on the next tick. The override returns true unless require_table_while_open is on.

WHY THE MENU TITLE IS THE MARKER. Because the menu reports MenuType.CRAFTING, the client cannot tell our grid from a real table by type. The title can: a real crafting table opens under container.crafting (CraftingTableBlock.CONTAINER_TITLE), the pocket grid under container.vanillaplusadditions.pocket_crafting. Deliberately NOT a menu-type check: Visual Workbench, which is installed in this pack, registers its own crafting menu type for the real table, so a type comparison would pass here by coincidence and break in a pack without it. Weak spot to be aware of: a mod that rewrites screen titles would defeat the marker.

ESC RETURN IS NOT A RACE, AND IT IS PROVABLE FROM THE PACKET ORDER. PocketCraftingScreen.onClose() calls super.onClose() first, which runs AbstractContainerScreen.onClose -> LocalPlayer.closeContainer(): that sends ServerboundContainerClosePacket, then clientSideCloseContainer() sets containerMenu = inventoryMenu and clears the screen. Only then does the override set a fresh InventoryScreen, which binds exactly that inventoryMenu. Clicks in the new screen address containerId 0, and the close packet went out earlier on the same ordered connection. Server side, doCloseContainer() -> removed() empties the grid back into the inventory through our access. One cosmetic artefact remains: a single frame with no screen (mouse grab) between the two, unavoidable because LocalPlayer.closeContainer calls setScreen(null) itself.

SERVER SIDE RE-VALIDATES EVERYTHING. The packet carries only a slot index, and it is not carried for convenience: without it the packet would be a free "open me a crafting grid anywhere" for any client. openGrid() checks that the player is not creative or spectator, that the index is in range of the menu the player actually has open, that slot.container is the player's own Inventory object - an identity check, which also rules out the chest half of a container screen (and rules out the inventory menu's own 2x2 grid and result slot, both backed by a transient container; main inventory, hotbar, armour and offhand all share the one Inventory object, and of those only the armour slots cannot hold a crafting table in the first place - the offhand can, and opening from there is intentionally allowed), and that the item in that slot really is a crafting table.

OPTIONAL NETWORK CHANNEL. The registrar uses .optional() and the client guards the send with connection.hasChannel(). Same reasoning as battle_dogs: NetworkComponentNegotiator fails the whole handshake over a non-optional channel the other side lacks, and the client is disconnected as incompatible. A server running only vpa_pocket_crafting would throw out every vanilla player over a convenience window. Note that item_vault_viewer and overpacked_extensions do register non-optional channels, so games2 already requires VPA client-side in practice - that is a reason not to add a third, not a reason to match them.

SHIFT IS LEFT ALONE. Shift-right-click stays vanilla's quick-move. The trigger also requires the slot's container to be the player Inventory, so the inventory's own crafting slots and armour slots never respond.

THE TABLE IS NEVER CONSUMED and never placed. What the grid gives you is the 3x3 recipes without putting a block down, using it and mining it again.

MOUSE TWEAKS COEXISTENCE, VERIFIED FROM BYTECODE. MouseTweaksNeo.onGuiMouseClickedPre listens on the same event and can cancel in principle, but all four return paths of Main.onMouseClicked are iconst_0/ireturn - it never cancels. Its right-click drag only arms when player.containerMenu.getCarried() is non-empty, so require_empty_carried puts us in the one branch where it does nothing. Visual Workbench, Easy Magic and Easy Anvils are all block-bound (CraftingTableWithInventoryBlock, EnchantmentTableWithInventoryBlock, AnvilWithInventoryBlock) and never touch InventoryScreen.

NOT MODELLED ON EASY SHULKER BOXES, DESPITE THE REQUEST. That mod opens no screen at all: fuzs.iteminteractions renders the contents as a tooltip inside the existing inventory screen and routes clicks through ItemStack.overrideStackedOnOther / overrideOtherStackedOnMe, i.e. through vanilla's already-synchronised slot-click path, which is why it has no "return to the previous screen" problem to solve. A crafting grid needs real recipe resolution and a ResultSlot, so that trick does not carry. What was taken from it is the event and reading the hovered slot.

THE TOOLTIP IS GATED ON THE SCREEN, NOT ON THE ITEM. ItemTooltipEvent fires wherever a tooltip is assembled - the creative menu, a chest, EMI's recipe panel, a held item - but the trigger only works in InventoryScreen. The handler therefore checks Minecraft.getInstance().screen before adding the line, so the hint appears exactly where acting on it does something. Appended rather than inserted, so it lands below the mod name line, matching where Easy Shulker Boxes puts its own.

OPENING FROM ANY CONTAINER SCREEN (added for beta.102, Gerry: it should work in all inventories, survival only). The trigger is any AbstractContainerScreen except a CraftingScreen (the real table's and our own), with the player neither creative nor spectator - in creative, E opens CreativeModeInventoryScreen, which is itself an AbstractContainerScreen and would otherwise qualify. Slot.index is the MENU index (AbstractContainerMenu.addSlot assigns slot.index = slots.size()), so the same packet works unchanged for a chest menu: the server resolves it against player.containerMenu, whatever that is.

GOING BACK INTO A CONTAINER NEEDS A MIXIN. A player has exactly one containerMenu, so ServerPlayer.openMenu closes the chest (closeContainer: close packet + doCloseContainer -> removed, lid shuts) before opening the grid. To return, the server must open it again, and an open menu does not know its provider. ServerPlayerMenuMemoryMixin therefore records, at RETURN of openMenu(MenuProvider, Consumer<RegistryFriendlyByteBuf>), the containerId, the provider and the extra-data writer. One hook is enough: NeoForge's patched ServerPlayer makes vanilla openMenu(MenuProvider) delegate to that overload, and IPlayerExtension.openMenu(provider, BlockPos) funnels into it too. The duck interface MenuMemory and the RememberedMenu record live in modules/pocket_crafting/menu, not in the mixin package, because classes in a mixin package must not be referenced directly.

THE ALLOW-LIST IS THE SAFETY BOUNDARY. Replaying a provider is only done when the recorded containerId still matches the open menu (a horse inventory is opened by openHorseInventory and never passes through openMenu, so it mismatches and falls back) and its menu type is in return_menu_types. getType() throws UnsupportedOperationException for menus built without a type and is caught. Not every provider survives a second call: OverpackedGuiBridge, for one, backs Overpacked's screen with a transient entity it discards on close, and Overpacked's client factory dereferences level.getEntity(id) without a null check - NeoForge answers that NullPointerException by disconnecting the client. Defaults are vanilla storage and processing blocks only. Ender chest note: reopening works, but PlayerEnderChestContainer.activeChest was cleared on the first close, so the lid does not animate on the way back.

TWO TITLE KEYS INSTEAD OF A PACKET. The server decides where Escape leads at the moment it opens the grid and encodes it in the title: container.vanillaplusadditions.pocket_crafting (back to the inventory) or container.vanillaplusadditions.pocket_crafting.return (back into the container). Both translate to "Crafting". The decision thus travels inside the same open-screen packet as the window, so it cannot arrive late, early or not at all.

THE RETURN REQUEST IS GUARDED. return_from_pocket_crafting carries no data - a client cannot name a container. The pending target is stored per player UUID when the grid opens, stamped with the server tick in PocketCraftingMenu.removed(), honoured once (removed from the map on use), only within RETURN_WINDOW_TICKS = 40 of that close, only while containerMenu == inventoryMenu and not creative/spectator, and dropped on PlayerLoggedOutEvent. Right after openMenu the reopened menu's stillValid() is checked and the container is closed again if it fails - this runs on the server thread inside the packet handler, so no client click can reach the menu first. Without that check a player who had walked away could get one tick of access to an out-of-reach chest (ChestMenu.stillValid is a 4-block-plus-reach distance test via Container.stillValidBlockEntity).

AUDIBLE SIDE EFFECT. The container really is closed and reopened, so chests and barrels play their close sound when the grid opens and their open sound on the way back.
oneLiner: Right-click a crafting table you are carrying - in your inventory or in your half of any open chest, barrel or furnace - and the ordinary crafting window opens on the spot, recipe book and all, with Escape taking you back to where you were instead of dropping you into the world.
shortDescription: Right-click a crafting table in your inventory to open the 3x3 crafting grid
